overviewHtml:
This graded quiz assesses your understanding of Merleau-Ponty's account of the body-subject. You'll be asked about the body schema and motor intentionality, the phantom limb and the Schneider case, and habit and incorporation.

Note: Aim for a score of 80 percent or higher. If you score lower, use the feedback to review the topics you missed, then retake the quiz.

forms.stemHtml: Why does Merleau-Ponty say you don't need to find your hand before moving it, though you must find a cup before moving it?

options.html: Because the hand is lighter and easier to move than the cup
options.text: Because the hand is lighter and easier to move than the cup
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the body as object and one's own body.

options.html: Because one's own body is given kinaesthetically, from within
options.text: Because one's own body is given kinaesthetically, from within
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! I move my body directly, not as an object located and then displaced.

options.html: Because the brain keeps a constant visual image of the hand
options.text: Because the brain keeps a constant visual image of the hand
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the body as object and one's own body.

options.html: Because the cup is outside the body schema's reach
options.text: Because the cup is outside the body schema's reach
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the body as object and one's own body.

forms.stemHtml: Why is Colin Smith's translation of Phenomenology of Perception a known source of confusion about the body schema?

options.html: It omits Merleau-Ponty's chapter on the body
options.text: It omits Merleau-Ponty's chapter on the body
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the body schema from Head and Holmes to Gallagher.

options.html: It sometimes calls the schema a "body image"
options.text: It sometimes calls the schema a "body image"
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! "Body image" suggests a picture of the body, which is what Merleau-Ponty denies the schema is.

options.html: It translates "body schema" as "lived body"
options.text: It translates "body schema" as "lived body"
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the body schema from Head and Holmes to Gallagher.

options.html: It was published before the term was invented
options.text: It was published before the term was invented
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the body schema from Head and Holmes to Gallagher.

forms.stemHtml: What is Merleau-Ponty's term for the space of one's own body, organized by tasks and possible actions rather than coordinates? Enter three words.

options.html: spatiality of situation
options.text: spatiality of situation
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! It's contrasted with spatiality of position, the coordinate space of objects.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on body schema, spatiality of situation, and motor intentionality.

forms.stemHtml: Why does Merleau-Ponty reject a mixed physiological-and-psychological theory of the phantom limb?

options.html: Because neither kind of explanation captures anything
options.text: Because neither kind of explanation captures anything
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on phantom limbs and anosognosia.

options.html: Because the two kinds of fact have no common ground
options.text: Because the two kinds of fact have no common ground
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Physiological and psychological facts belong to different orders, so a mixed theory can't join them.

options.html: Because phantom limbs are too rare to study
options.text: Because phantom limbs are too rare to study
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on phantom limbs and anosognosia.

options.html: Because only physiology can be tested empirically
options.text: Because only physiology can be tested empirically
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on phantom limbs and anosognosia.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are concrete movements, in Merleau-Ponty's sense? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Taking a handkerchief from your pocket to use it
options.text: Taking a handkerchief from your pocket to use it
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! It answers to an actual practical situation.

options.html: Swatting a fly that has landed on your arm
options.text: Swatting a fly that has landed on your arm
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! It answers to a real demand.

options.html: Imitating a gesture that someone demonstrates
options.text: Imitating a gesture that someone demonstrates
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on grasping and pointing.

options.html: Tracing a circle in the air when asked
options.text: Tracing a circle in the air when asked
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on grasping and pointing.

forms.stemHtml: What is Merleau-Ponty's term for the layer of settled capacities built up over a lifetime, which projects a field of practical possibilities onto the world? Enter two words.

options.html: habitual body
options.text: habitual body
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! In the phantom limb, the habitual body diverges from the body at this moment.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the habitual body and the body at this moment.

forms.stemHtml: A woman wearing a hat with a tall feather passes through doorways without catching it. What does Merleau-Ponty take this to show?

options.html: That she calculates the doorway's height each time
options.text: That she calculates the doorway's height each time
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on habit as motor knowledge.

options.html: That her body senses the feather's extent
options.text: That her body senses the feather's extent
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The body's sense of its own extent has grown to include the feather.

options.html: That she remembers the doorway from past visits
options.text: That she remembers the doorway from past visits
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on habit as motor knowledge.

options.html: That the feather has become a reflex trigger
options.text: That the feather has become a reflex trigger
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on habit as motor knowledge.

forms.stemHtml: A new cane user feels pressure in the palm; an experienced one feels the curb. What has changed?

options.html: The cane has become longer with use
options.text: The cane has become longer with use
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the blind person's cane.

options.html: The cane has been incorporated into the body schema
options.text: The cane has been incorporated into the body schema
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The cane is no longer perceived for itself. Its tip has become an area of sensitivity.

options.html: The user now calculates the cane's position faster
options.text: The user now calculates the cane's position faster
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the blind person's cane.

options.html: The user's hand has lost its sense of touch
options.text: The user's hand has lost its sense of touch
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the blind person's cane.

forms.stemHtml: An experienced organist has an hour to prepare on an unfamiliar organ. What happens in that hour, on Merleau-Ponty's account?

options.html: He learns a list of the new stop positions
options.text: He learns a list of the new stop positions
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the typist and the organist.

options.html: His body schema is rearranged to include the instrument
options.text: His body schema is rearranged to include the instrument
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! He settles into the organ's expressive space, and habit rearranges his body schema.

options.html: He forms new reflexes for each pedal
options.text: He forms new reflexes for each pedal
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the typist and the organist.

options.html: He mentally rehearses each piece without playing
options.text: He mentally rehearses each piece without playing
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the typist and the organist.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following describe habit, on Merleau-Ponty's account? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: A knowledge in the hands
options.text: A knowledge in the hands
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Habit is motor knowledge.

options.html: Neither reflex nor intellectual knowledge
options.text: Neither reflex nor intellectual knowledge
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Merleau-Ponty rejects both classical accounts.

options.html: A rearrangement of the body schema
options.text: A rearrangement of the body schema
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Acquiring a habit changes the body's sense of its possibilities.

options.html: A set of rules stored for later use
options.text: A set of rules stored for later use
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on habit as motor knowledge.

options.html: A narrowing of existence into routine
options.text: A narrowing of existence into routine
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the blind person's cane.

forms.stemHtml: Reaching for a cup, where is the movement directed, on Merleau-Ponty's account?

options.html: At a location calculated in objective coordinates
options.text: At a location calculated in objective coordinates
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on body schema, spatiality of situation, and motor intentionality.

options.html: At the cup itself, through motor intentionality
options.text: At the cup itself, through motor intentionality
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The cup solicits the reach, and the movement is directed at the thing, not at a coordinate.

options.html: At a mental image of the cup formed beforehand
options.text: At a mental image of the cup formed beforehand
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on body schema, spatiality of situation, and motor intentionality.

options.html: At the muscles that will carry out the reach
options.text: At the muscles that will carry out the reach
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on body schema, spatiality of situation, and motor intentionality.

forms.stemHtml: A patient who has lost proprioceptive input below the neck can still move, but only by watching his limbs and controlling each movement. What does Gallagher take this to show?

options.html: That the body image and body schema are the same system
options.text: That the body image and body schema are the same system
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading comparing body schema and body image.

options.html: That the two systems can come apart
options.text: That the two systems can come apart
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Without the body schema's normal support, the patient relies on vision and attention to do its work.

options.html: That movement never depends on the body schema
options.text: That movement never depends on the body schema
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading comparing body schema and body image.

options.html: That vision is the basis of all bodily awareness
options.text: That vision is the basis of all bodily awareness
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading comparing body schema and body image.

forms.stemHtml: What is Merleau-Ponty's French term, usually translated "one's own body," for the body as I live it, the permanent point of view from which I perceive and act? Enter two words.

options.html: corps propre
options.text: corps propre
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Corps propre names the lived body as a point of view, not an object.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the body as object and one's own body.

forms.stemHtml: On Merleau-Ponty's account, what does the phantom limb keep open?

options.html: A memory of the injury that caused the loss
options.text: A memory of the injury that caused the loss
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the habitual body and the body at this moment.

options.html: A field of practical possibilities for the missing limb
options.text: A field of practical possibilities for the missing limb
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The habitual body still projects a world that calls for the limb.

options.html: A nerve pathway that can be surgically repaired
options.text: A nerve pathway that can be surgically repaired
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the habitual body and the body at this moment.

options.html: A belief that the limb will grow back
options.text: A belief that the limb will grow back
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the habitual body and the body at this moment.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are features of the intentional arc? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: It projects our past and future around us
options.text: It projects our past and future around us
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The arc projects our past, future, human setting, and situation.

options.html: It unifies perception, movement, and understanding
options.text: It unifies perception, movement, and understanding
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A disturbance of the arc affects all three together.

options.html: It goes slack in Schneider, on Merleau-Ponty's reading
options.text: It goes slack in Schneider, on Merleau-Ponty's reading
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The world no longer projects possibilities beyond the immediate.

options.html: It's an explicit plan formed before acting
options.text: It's an explicit plan formed before acting
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the intentional arc and the reliability of the Schneider case.

options.html: It's a specific circuit in the brain
options.text: It's a specific circuit in the brain
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the intentional arc and the reliability of the Schneider case.

forms.stemHtml: What is the term for the failure or refusal to acknowledge a paralyzed or impaired limb as one's own, which Merleau-Ponty pairs with the phantom limb? Enter one word.

options.html: anosognosia
options.text: anosognosia
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! One patient keeps a limb that's gone. The other disowns a limb that's still there.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on phantom limbs and anosognosia.

forms.stemHtml: Why does Merleau-Ponty reject the reflex account of habit?

options.html: Because habits never involve repetition
options.text: Because habits never involve repetition
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on habit as motor knowledge.

options.html: Because habits meet new situations flexibly
options.text: Because habits meet new situations flexibly
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A typist types new words, and a driver handles new roads. Fixed reflexes can't explain this.

options.html: Because reflexes are always conscious
options.text: Because reflexes are always conscious
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on habit as motor knowledge.

options.html: Because habits can always be stated as rules
options.text: Because habits can always be stated as rules
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on habit as motor knowledge.

forms.stemHtml: Merleau-Ponty says habit expresses our power to "dilate" our being in the world. What does he mean?

options.html: That habits narrow our existence into routine
options.text: That habits narrow our existence into routine
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the blind person's cane.

options.html: That habits enlarge existence through new instruments
options.text: That habits enlarge existence through new instruments
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Every new habit is an expansion: the body's world grows as the body itself grows.

options.html: That habits make the body physically larger
options.text: That habits make the body physically larger
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the blind person's cane.

options.html: That habits let us escape our situation
options.text: That habits let us escape our situation
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the blind person's cane.

forms.stemHtml: In the comparison of accounts of skill, what distinguishes mechanical association?

options.html: It treats the tool as part of the lived body
options.text: It treats the tool as part of the lived body
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on peripersonal space and tool use.

options.html: It treats skill as rules known and applied
options.text: It treats skill as rules known and applied
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on peripersonal space and tool use.

options.html: It treats skill as learned cue-response links
options.text: It treats skill as learned cue-response links
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Mechanical association links fixed cues to fixed movements, so it handles new situations poorly.

options.html: It treats skill as a rearranged body schema
options.text: It treats skill as a rearranged body schema
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on peripersonal space and tool use.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are examples of incorporation? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Feeling the road's texture through a car's tires
options.text: Feeling the road's texture through a car's tires
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The car has been taken into the body schema.

options.html: Feeling the paper's grain at a pen's tip
options.text: Feeling the paper's grain at a pen's tip
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Sensation is felt at the tool's point of contact.

options.html: Reading a manual on how to use a new drill
options.text: Reading a manual on how to use a new drill
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the blind person's cane.

options.html: Feeling a heavy bag's pressure on your palm
options.text: Feeling a heavy bag's pressure on your palm
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the blind person's cane.

forms.stemHtml: Head and Holmes proposed a "postural schema." What did it do, on their account?

options.html: It stored a conscious picture of the body's appearance
options.text: It stored a conscious picture of the body's appearance
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the body schema from Head and Holmes to Gallagher.

options.html: It controlled reflexes in the spinal cord
options.text: It controlled reflexes in the spinal cord
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the body schema from Head and Holmes to Gallagher.

options.html: It registered posture changes against a standard
options.text: It registered posture changes against a standard
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The postural schema was a continually updated standard, working largely outside awareness.

options.html: It represented the body's beliefs about itself
options.text: It represented the body's beliefs about itself
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the body schema from Head and Holmes to Gallagher.

forms.stemHtml: Which statement best describes the status of the body schema vs. body image distinction today?

options.html: It's universally accepted and settled
options.text: It's universally accepted and settled
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading comparing body schema and body image.

options.html: It's been abandoned by researchers
options.text: It's been abandoned by researchers
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading comparing body schema and body image.

options.html: It's influential but still debated
options.text: It's influential but still debated
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Critics argue that there are more than two systems and that the labels hide variation.

options.html: It applies only to patients, not to healthy people
options.text: It applies only to patients, not to healthy people
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading comparing body schema and body image.

forms.stemHtml: In Gallagher's distinction, what is the term for a system of perceptions, attitudes, and beliefs about one's own body? Enter two words.

options.html: body image
options.text: body image
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Gallagher distinguishes the body image from the body schema.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the body schema from Head and Holmes to Gallagher.

forms.stemHtml: Why does Merleau-Ponty reject the intellectualist reading of Schneider?

options.html: Because Schneider's thinking was completely normal
options.text: Because Schneider's thinking was completely normal
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on grasping and pointing.

options.html: Because the deficit shows up in how he moves
options.text: Because the deficit shows up in how he moves
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! If only a symbolic function of thought were lost, the deficit should be purely cognitive. It isn't.

options.html: Because Schneider could point but not grasp
options.text: Because Schneider could point but not grasp
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on grasping and pointing.

options.html: Because intellectualism can't explain vision
options.text: Because intellectualism can't explain vision
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on grasping and pointing.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are reasonable responses to doubts about the Schneider case? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The argument's pattern also rests on other cases
options.text: The argument's pattern also rests on other cases
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The phantom limb supports the same pattern.

options.html: Everyday experience shows the scratch-and-point contrast
options.text: Everyday experience shows the scratch-and-point contrast
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Anyone can notice the difference without a clinical case.

options.html: The case has been fully confirmed, so doubts are baseless
options.text: The case has been fully confirmed, so doubts are baseless
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the intentional arc and the reliability of the Schneider case.

options.html: The case is irrelevant to the intentional arc
options.text: The case is irrelevant to the intentional arc
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the intentional arc and the reliability of the Schneider case.

forms.stemHtml: What is the German term for pointing, the movement Schneider reportedly couldn't perform on command? Enter one word.

options.html: Zeigen
options.text: Zeigen
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Schneider could grasp (Greifen) but not point (Zeigen).

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on grasping and pointing.

forms.stemHtml: What does Merleau-Ponty mean by saying the body "understands" when it acquires a habit?

options.html: That the mind has stored a new rule for the body
options.text: That the mind has stored a new rule for the body
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on habit as motor knowledge.

options.html: That it grasps the fit between aim and performance
options.text: That it grasps the fit between aim and performance
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Bodily understanding is the body's grasp of the agreement between what it intends and what it does.

options.html: That the body has learned to follow instructions
options.text: That the body has learned to follow instructions
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on habit as motor knowledge.

options.html: That the habit can now be explained in words
options.text: That the habit can now be explained in words
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on habit as motor knowledge.

forms.stemHtml: How should research on peripersonal space and tool use relate to Merleau-Ponty's account, as the comparison presents it?

options.html: As a proof that his account is correct
options.text: As a proof that his account is correct
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on peripersonal space and tool use.

options.html: As a refutation of his account
options.text: As a refutation of his account
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on peripersonal space and tool use.

options.html: As an outside view that fits his inside description
options.text: As an outside view that fits his inside description
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The findings are a pointer, not a proof. They describe brain representation, while Merleau-Ponty described lived experience.

options.html: As unrelated, since it studies monkeys only
options.text: As unrelated, since it studies monkeys only
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on peripersonal space and tool use.

forms.stemHtml: Which example best shows the difference between incorporation and extension?

options.html: Incorporation is the cane; extension is the hand
options.text: Incorporation is the cane; extension is the hand
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the blind person's cane.

options.html: Incorporation is the process; extension the result
options.text: Incorporation is the process; extension the result
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Incorporation names the process, and extension names the enlarged reach that results.

options.html: Incorporation applies to cars; extension to canes
options.text: Incorporation applies to cars; extension to canes
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the blind person's cane.

options.html: Incorporation is conscious; extension is unconscious
options.text: Incorporation is conscious; extension is unconscious
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the blind person's cane.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are claims about peripersonal space that the reading on tool use presents? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: It's the space within reach around the body
options.text: It's the space within reach around the body
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Peripersonal space surrounds the body.

options.html: It can expand to include a held tool
options.text: It can expand to include a held tool
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Research suggests tool use can extend the zone treated as near.

options.html: The findings are debated in their details
options.text: The findings are debated in their details
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! They're a pointer, not a proof.

options.html: It's fixed at the skin and never changes
options.text: It's fixed at the skin and never changes
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on peripersonal space and tool use.

options.html: It's the same as the body image
options.text: It's the same as the body image
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on peripersonal space and tool use.
